body:
A Leeds-based private equity investor has acquired £200m-turnover housebuilder Weston Group, Building’s sister title Housing Today can reveal.

Endless LLP has bought a majority stake in the Essex-based business, which reported a pre-tax loss of £4.5m in its most recent accounts

The housebuilder will retain its senior management team led by chief executive Peter Gore.

The deal means chair and founder Bob Weston is no longer a person of significant control at the group and will take a step back from day-to-day running of the business although a spokesperson said he will remain “actively” involved with the firm.

No details of the amount Endless has paid for the business, which Weston set up in 1987, have been revealed but it is expected the move will see the housebuilder given a cash boost.

Endless, founded in 2005, has acquired more than 100 firms and raised £1.5bn in capital. It describes itself as a funder that provides “a safe first home for businesses moving away from family ownership”, while “remaining respectful of heritage and brand”.

Gore said: “This marks an exciting new growth chapter for Weston Homes. With Endless’s backing, we have the investment and support to build on the strengths of the group, deliver our existing developments and invest in new opportunities for the future.

“We have a strong brand, an experienced team and a clear ambition to grow the business sustainably over the coming years, while continuing to deliver the quality and standards our customers associate with Weston Homes.”
